🧠 Ultrathink & output style

Ultrathink spends an unusually large thinking budget once, on the opening of a hard piece of work — the environment it needs, the constraints, and the first prompt to hand a builder. That is the one place a huge budget reliably pays, because every later call inherits the framing. The full trace is kept, because a plan you cannot audit is only an assertion.

Output style

Applies to every model call this app makes — advisors, builder, assistant, bots and agents alike. A style only shrinks output tokens: it costs input tokens on every call and does not touch reasoning tokens, so on short calls it can cost more than it saves. The ledger below measures both sides instead of quoting a headline number.

🎛 Reasoning Ops — who thinks, when, how deeply, and for how much

Every advisor pass is governed by a dollar cap. Glassbox Jet converts that cap into a token budget using the model's live price, then chooses how tersely it must write to fit. Set a pass to 5¢ and Fable answers in caveman telegram that still carries every fact the builder needs; set it to 50¢ and it writes full architecture.

Frontier advisors

Operation spread — multiple small passes per builder round

👁 Vision advisor — eyes for builders that can't see

Captures the real rendered frame from the Studio preview and sends it to a model that can see images. Built for strong-but-blind builders. WebGL capture is forced to work by patching preserveDrawingBuffer before the page's own scripts run.

🔧 Builders

Specialist sub-agents run after the main build, each patching only its own dimension

Discipline & efficiency

Hard checks on the artifact itself, applied before any judgement counts: files parse, an entry file exists, no // rest of code elisions, balanced braces, a closing </html>, zero runtime errors, and every objective explicitly verified. A model cannot talk its way past these.

Forwards the full chain-of-thought on round 1, then a compacted head afterwards — the brief and fragments already carry its conclusions. This is what keeps a 20-round run affordable.

⚡ Efficiency

The largest cost lever available. Every round re-sends the same system prompt, skills, brain notes and files — only the fixes change. Cached reads bill at 0.1× on Anthropic and DeepSeek and 0.25–0.5× on OpenAI, and production reports put the saving at 41–80% of input cost. Glassbox Jet now orders every prompt so the unchanging part is one contiguous prefix, because a cache matches on an exact prefix and one early character invalidates all of it.

🗳 Functional voting

Generate several candidates and pick the winner by what the code does, not what it looks like. Text-similarity voting is the obvious version and the research says it backfires — majority vote measurably reduced accuracy on hard problems, because model errors are strongly correlated and extra samples entrench a wrong answer. Judging by executed behaviour avoids that, and took one open model from 37.7% to 52.7%.

Costs N× the builder pass, so it is worth it on a round that keeps failing rather than on every round. Needs Studio on, since candidates must actually run.

🧭 Route by what things actually cost

Cheap per token is not cheap per finished thing. With enough completed tasks, Glassbox Jet can pick the model with the best measured cost-per-completed-task for this kind of project — and it says plainly when it has too little evidence to have an opinion, rather than guessing.

♻️ Loop until perfect

Keeps running rounds until every gate you have switched on passes — and stops honestly when it stops making progress. A loop without stall detection is just a way to spend money while you sleep, so this one watches the score and gives up out loud when three rounds in a row achieve nothing.

“Flat” means the score moved less than 1.5 points across those rounds.

🌐 Web access — give any model live internet

OpenRouter can put any model online, not just the ones with built-in search. Domain filters are the important part: they make “prefer arXiv and university sources” a hard constraint on the search itself rather than a polite request in a prompt.

🔭 Recon — research the latest before building anything

A model's training cutoff is the weakest link when you ask for a new feature, architecture or plugin — it will confidently hand you last year's answer. Recon spends one cheap online call first, finds what is current and what is actually adopted, scores every result on recency, authority, adoption and relevance, distils it from first principles, and hands that to the architect.

Recon only fires when the ask actually looks like a “what should I use / add / build” question — it stays out of the way otherwise.

🐝 Swarm — builders working in parallel instead of one after another

Splits the app by concern and runs several builders at once, each owning its own files and coordinating through a shared blackboard. Wall-clock time is the slowest member, not the sum — and each member can be a cheaper model because its slice is smaller. Members that need something from each other write a handshake instead of building it twice.

📱 Mobile QA gate

Runs each round at real phone viewports and blocks it on defects that only show up there. Findings become required fixes automatically.

⏱ Performance budget

Measured from the app actually running — frame rate, 95th-percentile frame time, long tasks, DOM size, heap. Exceeding a budget fails the round the same way a crash does.

🛡 Regression guard

Pin a golden snapshot in 📱 Devices once the build is good. After that, any check that passed then and fails now is a regression — reported explicitly and, with this on, enough to fail the round. This is what makes "don't break what works" enforceable rather than a polite request in a prompt.

👁 OCR — give the models eyes

Read a scanned PDF or a photograph of text entirely in this browser. No upload, no OCR API, no per-page charge, and once the model is cached it works offline. What it reads becomes searchable, and models can query it with ocr_search instead of guessing at a document they cannot see.

Everything Glassbox Jet can genuinely see. Each source is labelled with its real reach — a browser page cannot enumerate sessions on other machines or other accounts, so anything it cannot reach is shown as unreachable rather than invented.

💬 Comms — everything said, in one stream

Messages between you and the agents, and between the agents themselves. Anything you send to a running relay is picked up by the very next round as a top-priority instruction.

🗣 Standup

Before the expensive build, every active member says in one line what it is about to do, what is blocking it and what it needs from someone else. Two members claiming the same file shows up here instead of as a merge conflict three minutes later.

⬆ Escalation and delegation

A cheap model that knows when to ask for help beats an expensive one used for everything. Give the builder a stronger model it can consult: when it is stuck it emits an ===ASK FOR HELP=== block, only that question travels up, and only the answer comes back — you pay for a paragraph, not a whole extra build.

🌳 Run tree

Every model call as a span with a parent, so a run reads as a tree rather than a flat log. The shape is the diagnostic: a healthy run is broad and shallow; one that has gone wrong shows a single branch descending forever, or the same node over and over.

Where the tokens went

Reasoning tokens are billed as output but are not the answer. A model spending 80% of its output on thinking and 20% on the deliverable is a very different cost profile from the reverse, and until you split them the bill looks the same.

👍 Grade this run

The most useful prompt material there is, because it is specific and it is yours. Anything you note here is fed into later builds as a standing instruction.

↔ Run divergence

Two runs of the same task rarely fail in the same place, and the useful question is never whether they differ — it is where they stopped being the same. This aligns the two step sequences and marks the first point they part company, with what each step cost on either side.

⭐ Golden traces

Keep a run you were happy with and measure later ones against it. Cost and shape regressions are as real as output regressions and far easier to miss.

🔌 Connectors

GitHub over its REST API, and any MCP server. Two honest limits: a browser can only reach an HTTP MCP server directly if that server sends CORS headers (otherwise the bridge forwards it), and it can never start a local command server itself — those need the bridge, full stop.

🧪 A/B experiments

Run the same task under two configurations and compare what each actually cost to reach the same quality. This is the check the harness research found nobody had — which is how a real harness got 71% more expensive and 23% less effective without anyone noticing.

Record a variant after each run: it captures the spend, rounds and score of whatever just finished.

💰 Cost per completed task

The number that actually matters. Not tokens, not rounds, not score — what it costs to get one thing finished to your satisfaction, counting every failed attempt along the way. A task only counts as completed when you say it is.

Why this metric

A 2026 study of a real coding-agent harness (arXiv:2607.03691) tracked it across its own version history: the resolve rate fell from 39% to 30% while token use rose from 391K to 668K — 71% more expensive for 23% less effective. Every one of those regressions passed the project's existing automated checks, because those checks only ever asked “did it pass”, never “what did it cost to pass”.

That is the failure this tab exists to catch. If Glassbox Jet starts costing more per finished task, the trend above says so out loud.

🧠 The Brain — a growing folder of .md notes

Every round, every piece of research and every failure can be distilled into a short Markdown note. Notes you mark active are injected into later prompts, so the next build starts from what the last one learned. That loop is the whole point: the app gets better at your project the longer you use it, without retraining anything.

Notes are plain .md with YAML frontmatter — readable by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or you.

Set it up — entirely optional

Nothing is written anywhere until you pick one of these. On a phone, the zip is the right answer and works fine.

📁 A real folder

Desktop Chrome or Edge. Pick a folder once and the app writes each note straight into it as it is created — the closest thing to a live second brain on disk.

🔌 Via the bridge

If the local bridge is running it can write the notes to any path you name, including inside a git repo.

📦 A zip — works on iPhone

Notes accumulate inside the app and you export them whenever you like. iOS Files unzips natively, so on an iPhone or iPad this is the whole workflow — no folder API needed.

🗺️ The map it builds itself as you add notes

Every note is a node; links come from [[wikilinks]], shared tags, then kind. Drag to turn it, scroll to zoom, click a node to read it. The layout is deterministic, so the same brain always makes the same shape — it becomes something you recognise.

three.js is fetched from a CDN, so the WebGL version needs a connection. With no connection Glassbox Jet draws the same map with its own renderer — same layout, same maths, same interactions — so the map is never simply missing.

Notes

✏️ Edit Glassbox Jet's own source

This is the actual open-source HTML of the app you are using. It is read-only and inert until you arm it — an app that can rewrite itself by accident is a bug, not a feature.

Before you arm it: every apply snapshots the previous source first, so you can roll back to any earlier state from the history below. The source is also validated before writing — a truncated or structurally broken file is refused rather than saved.

Load the source

“Pick the file” uses the File System Access API to hold a read/write handle on GlassBox.html — that is what lets Apply save in place and reload. Without it, Apply downloads a new copy for you to swap in yourself. Safari and iOS only support the download route.

Each apply stores the full previous source, so any of these is a complete, exact rollback — not a partial diff. Thumbnails are best-effort; the source is the real artifact.

Searches live, restricted to sources worth trusting, and scores every result on recency, authority, adoption and relevance to what you asked. Findings can be saved into the Brain as notes, or turned straight into proposed edits to Glassbox Jet itself.

🚀 Ship it — GitHub & Vercel

        
Glassbox Jet is one HTML file with no build step, which makes it a static site
          already. This writes the small amount of scaffolding a host expects, and hands you the

🚀 Hand the finished work to another agent

        
Glassbox Jet is a waypoint, not a walled garden. A handoff carries the code plus everything that produced it — the brief, both reasoning traces, every review verdict, the changelog and the open problems — so the next tool starts informed instead of guessing. It writes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md, which is how Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and friends pick up project rules automatically.

🔮 Visualiser

        
One scene for everything with structure — knowledge graphs, brain notes,
          reasoning traces, skills, and the factory line. It reuses the Brain map's renderer pair,
          which means it inherits the offline fallback: three.js when it can be fetched, the
          built-in renderer when it cannot, same layout and same interactions either way, so
          the picture is never simply missing. Node size carries the win/loss record, so what you
          see says something true rather than only looking good. Click any node to open it.

        

          
          
          
        

        

        

      

      

        
💬 Ask about your knowledge

        
Ask what is actually in your Brain, graphs, skills and traces — and what
          to research or gather next. It is grounded in a real inventory assembled from your data,
          never in what a model imagines a knowledge base contains: a confident wrong inventory is
          worse than no answer, because you cannot tell it from a real one until you act on it.

🦥 Unsloth Desktop

        
Unsloth serves models through llama-server behind an authenticated local
          API and speaks two dialects on one port — OpenAI's
          /v1/chat/completions and Anthropic's
          /v1/messages. The port varies by install, so leave the base
          blank and this probes a ladder rather than guessing one and failing confusingly.

⚖️ Ollama vs Unsloth Desktop

        
Both run models on your own machine and neither replaces the other:
          Ollama is the simpler server, Unsloth is the workstation. The training, sandbox and
          diffusion rows are Unsloth's own documented features — this app cannot verify them
          from the browser, and does not pretend to. What it does verify is which
          endpoints answer and whether generation actually works.

Trending and top releases, live. Hugging Face only allows browser

          this says so rather than showing an empty list that looks like "no results".

        

          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🧑‍💻 Ask about your hardware

        
What a browser can see about this machine is limited and partly
          misleading — it cannot read VRAM at all, and Chrome caps reported RAM at 8 GB no

🏭 AI Software Factory

        
The loop that turns "stuff to do" into shipped change, with agents at the
          stations that used to be people. The claim this is built on: once an agent writes the
          code, review becomes the bottleneck — build drops from days to minutes while
          review still takes hours. So a factory that only speeds up building just makes a
          bigger pile of pull requests. You don't have too many PRs, you have too many bad
          PRs. Everything here is biased toward each item being correct before it reaches you.

        
Human attention pays off unevenly, so the line front-loads the four
          stations where it matters — product design, architecture, program design, vertical
          slices — and lets you gate any of them. Program design is the station most people
          skip, and skipping it is why output needs so much rework: the model ends up inventing
          the shape of the code while it is also writing it.

🕸 Knowledge graphs

        
A layer above the notes. Notes are flat text scored by word overlap — fine
          for “what did we learn”, useless for “what does this depend on” or “what did we already
          try that failed”. The graph stores relationships as typed and directional:
          A supersedes B and B supersedes A are opposite facts, and word-overlap
          retrieval cannot tell them apart. Edges carry provenance and confidence, decay when
          unconfirmed, and are reinforced when they sit on the path of a run that worked —
          so the graph is shaped by what actually succeeded, not by what was merely written down.

        

          
          
          
        

        

        

      

      

        
🩺 Graph health

        
The five numbers that say whether a graph is still worth injecting.
          Density under ~0.8 means it is a list wearing a graph's clothes — the relationships are
          the whole reason it exists. A graph only ever looks bigger; these say whether it
          is getting better.

        

        

      

      

        
🎓 Skills — selector, routing and YOLO

        
Every active skill is injected into every prompt, so loading them all
          costs the same instruction budget that frontier models measurably run out of at 150–200
          items. Selection is the feature, not the library. Auto matches locally first and
          only spends a model call when the cheap path is genuinely unsure — paying a model to
          choose a prompt would tax every request. In the chat window, type / to load one
          by hand.

Turn a repo into a skill

        
Not a spec for rebuilding it — a procedure for using it correctly:
          the conventions and the traps, which is what a model gets wrong about a library it
          half-remembers.

        

          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🔗 Memory bus — your CLIs read and write this Brain

        
Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, Hermes, Goose — anything that speaks
          MCP — can recall from this Brain, write lessons back, add typed relationships to the
          graphs, and audit the whole thing for the failure modes that actually degrade agent
          memory. The Brain lives in this tab's IndexedDB, which a subprocess cannot read, so it
          mirrors to a file the bridge owns; rev numbers keep a stale push from
          silently clobbering what an agent just learned.

        

          
          
          
        

        

        

        
Audit

        
Runs brain_audit through the same MCP server your CLIs use, so
          what you see here is exactly what Prime Agent sees. It checks the failure modes that
          actually degrade agent memory — contradictions with no winner, duplicates, stale
          unconfirmed claims, unsourced assertions, orphan nodes — and reports what each would
          cost if left alone. It demotes and expires; it never deletes.

        

          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🎚 Capability tiers — memory sized to the model

        
The counter-intuitive half: injecting more into a strong model makes
          it worse. Frontier models reliably follow only 150–200 instructions before
          adherence degrades, and every instruction competes with the model's own better defaults —
          so a stale rule forces Opus to arbitrate between your prompt and its judgement instead of
          just working. A weak model has the opposite problem and needs the code and the steps.
          Same graph, rendered differently.

        
TierBudgetItemsIncludes

          

        

          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🔬 Research → Plan → Implement

        
Discrete phases, each producing a persistent artifact — because
          human attention has wildly uneven leverage across them: bad research corrupts thousands
          of lines, a bad plan corrupts hundreds, bad code is just bad code. So review the
          research closely and the code loosely. Implement reads the plan, not the
          conversation that produced it. Specs are kept, not discarded — throwing them away and
          keeping only the code is keeping the binary and deleting the source.

        
Target context utilisation is 40–60%. Above that, quality falls off
          well before the hard limit; the compaction button writes a structured progress artifact
          before the window fills rather than letting a summariser fire under duress.

        

          
          
        

        

        

      

      

        
✦ What the memory actually did

        
Every time a prompt is assembled with the Brain and graph attached, this
          records which nodes fired, which paths were traversed, what each contributed — and what
          was withheld and why. Memory you cannot inspect is memory you eventually stop
          trusting and switch off.

        

        

      

      

        
🤝 Local AI Assist — checkpoint drop-ins

        
A stronger model supplies your local model between rounds: it works, pauses,
          the assistant looks at what it actually wrote and hands over code or a missing
          signature, then it resumes. You choose how many drop-ins.

        
Why it cannot get in the way. The assistant never receives a writable
          copy of the work and never returns the artifact, so it structurally cannot delete or
          overrule anything. Its material arrives inside a data fence that ranks your model's
          judgement above it. It is told to supply only what is missing and may answer
          “NOTHING NEEDED”. If it errors, the run continues untouched. This shape is deliberate:
          steering accuracy measurably collapses as helper count rises, and naive always-on
          broadcasting raises hallucination — so this defaults to one assistant behind a gate.

        

          
          
          
          
          
          
        

        

        
        

          
          
        

        

        

        

      

      

        
🔁 Long-horizon loops

        
A loop is a procedure with a gate, replayed every round so the next action
          is read rather than invented — which is what lets a small model run a long task at
          all. The gate is restated every single round on purpose: long-context degradation is
          measured, models miss things far more often late in a transcript than early, and
          repeating the invariant is the documented mitigation. The harness decides when the gate
          is met; the model never gets to declare itself finished.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        
LoopKindState

          

      

    


    

      

        
🛡 Lethal trifecta guard

        
An agent becomes dangerous in one nameable combination: access to
          private data + exposure to untrusted content + the ability to
          communicate externally. Any two are ordinarily fine. All three means a web page or
          a repo file is in a position to instruct your agent to exfiltrate your data — and nothing
          in the model layer reliably stops that, because the instruction arrives as data the model
          was told to read. This tracks capability rather than intent, because you cannot detect a
          malicious instruction reliably but you absolutely can detect that one would now work.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🔐 Tool permissions by phase

        
Which tools exist should depend on the phase. A planning phase has no
          business writing files; a verify phase has no business repairing the thing it is meant to
          judge. Removing a tool from the menu is far more reliable than instructing a model not to
          reach for it.

        

          
          

          
        

        

      

      

        
🐤 Model drift canaries

        
A model id is not a fixed thing. Providers repoint an id at a new build or
          change a default, nothing announces it, and your harness quietly starts behaving
          differently while you blame your own prompt. Pin a canary, re-run it later, and compare
          against the baseline. Similarity is reported rather than pass/fail — output is never
          byte-stable, so a sharp drop is the signal, not any single run.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        
CanaryBaselineLast

          

      

      

        
🩺 Refusal & stop diagnostics

        
A short or empty response has three very different causes that want opposite
          responses: a length cut wants continuation, a filter stop wants a different
          provider, and a genuine decline wants a clearer request. Guessing wrong wastes a
          round every time. Paste a response to classify it.

        

          
          
        

        
        

      

      

        
🔥 Context budget heatmap

        
Every prompt is assembled from parts, and it is normally impossible to see
          which part is eating the budget. A prompt size that only ever climbs is the documented way
          a harness silently gets worse — and you cannot fix what you cannot attribute.

        

          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🔔 Run notifications

        
Autonomous runs are long, and watching a tab for twenty minutes defeats the
          point of one. This tells you when something finished, failed or is waiting on you —
          including when the tab is in the background, which is exactly when it matters.

🔩 Reverse engineering

        
Turn something that already exists back into the specification that would
          rebuild it. It reads the real tree and the real key files through your GitHub
          connector rather than asking a model what it remembers about the project — recollection of a
          repo is exactly the confident, stale answer this app exists to avoid. The output is a
          specification to implement, not a copy of the source.

        

          
          
          
        

        

          
          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🔬 Autoresearch — bounded self-improvement

        
The one finding that matters from the recursive-self-improvement work:
          agents improve reliably only where the outcome is mechanically verifiable. Where
          the metric is a judgement, self-improvement degenerates into a model awarding itself
          points. So this loop is narrow on purpose — it mutates harness configuration, runs
          your evaluation task, and keeps a change only if a number Glassbox Jet measured itself moved
          the right way. The model proposes; arithmetic decides. It cannot rewrite its own source,
          and it can only touch an explicit allowlist of settings, so every experiment is
          reversible by assignment. Kept changes are written to the Brain and the graph with
          verified provenance.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        
        

        

      

    


    

      

        
🎚 Models

        
One place to decide which models do what, saved as presets you can
          apply anywhere instead of retyping ids in six tabs. A preset names the four roles this app
          actually routes to — architect, builder, critic and a cheap model for the small jobs — so
          switching from “fast and cheap” to “careful and expensive” is one click rather than a
          settings audit.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🧬 Mixture of Agents

        
Several models propose, an aggregator decides, and it repeats in layers —
          each layer sees the previous aggregate and is told to improve on it, not agree with
          it. That instruction is load-bearing: an aggregator that averages its inputs
          reproduces the majority-vote failure where correlated model errors reinforce each other
          instead of being caught. Select Mixture of Agents in the Assistant to use it.

        

      

      

        
📌 Where each model is used

        
Every place this app picks a model on your behalf, and what it is currently
          set to. If a run cost more than you expected, this is the list that explains why.

        

      

    


    

      

        

          
          

        

        

          

            

            
            
            
            
          

          

          

          

          

            
            

              
              
            

          

        

      

    


    

      

      

        
🧠 Brain console

        
Working memory with a lifecycle. Notes can expire, can be marked
          provisional, can be scoped to the agents that actually need them, and can carry the
          reference material that makes them actionable. Mistakes are separate and unconditional.

        

      

      

        
📥 Import a brain from elsewhere

        
Granular, Obsidian, Logseq, a Notion export, or any folder of markdown.
          They all converged on the same idea — plain files linked with
          [[wikilinks]] — so this is one importer, not five. Detection
          is about the shape around the markdown: a .obsidian directory,
          pages/ and journals/, a
          brain/BRAIN.md front door, or 32-hex Notion suffixes.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        
Blank template files that ship with these tools are
          skipped — importing Granular's eight empty scaffolds would bury your real notes.

        

      

      

        
🔬 Analyse this brain

        
The useful question is not whether the brain is big but whether it is
          shaped for the way this harness reads it — the harness injects a budgeted slice
          into every prompt, so what a reader hits first, what is reachable, and what is
          duplicated all cost real tokens. The report proposes edits to the brain and
          changes to the harness, because sometimes the setup should bend to the notes.

        

          
          
          
        

        

        

      

      

        
🧭 Curator & sub-agents

        
One pass reads the whole knowledge base, decides which agents need each
          note, attaches the reference nodes that must travel with it, and proposes the sub-agents
          to carry open work forward. It proposes; applying is a separate, explicit step —
          a model that could silently rewrite its own knowledge base could launder a bad
          conclusion into permanent fact.

        

          
          
          
        

        

        

        

      

      

        
🌙 Dreaming

        
A consolidation pass over what actually happened recently, plus what the
          outside world published. It builds a tree of candidate ideas and prunes it — an
          idea generator without a pruning step is just a note-count generator. Dropped branches
          keep their reason so the pruning can be judged.

        

          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
✗ Mistakes — never twice

        
Injected into every future build regardless of how well it matches the
          task, because the mistake you are about to repeat rarely shares vocabulary with the
          task that repeats it.

        

          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
📼 Reasoning trace vault

        
Every capture is logged here automatically the moment it completes —
          before you decide anything — so starting the next project can no longer throw away
          thinking you already paid for. Traces are deliberately not auto-written into the
          Brain: raw transcripts would flood it and make every later injection worse. Promoting
          one is a deliberate act.

        

        

      

      

        
🔭 Research sessions

        
Kept the moment results arrive, grouped by the search that produced them.
          Reopen an old search like a saved conversation and add what you want to the Brain.

        

      

    


    

      

        
🔍 Glass-Pane

        
Everything this machine is doing on your behalf, in one place — every model
          call, every MCP and connector tool call, every local CLI, every terminal, every agent and
          sub-agent, and OpenHands if it is running. It reads the same event log the rest of the app
          writes through, so it cannot drift from the truth by keeping its own copy.

        

        

          

          
          
          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
📎 Paperclip

        
Paperclip (MIT, self-hosted) runs a team of agents as a company — goals,
          employees, tasks, budgets. Its REST surface is not published in its README or product
          docs, so rather than hardcode routes that would fail confusingly against whatever
          version you installed, this probes and tells you exactly what answered. Point the
          three paths at whichever endpoints are real on your install.

        

          
          
          
        

        

          
          
          
          
        

        

        

      

      

        
Live on this device

        
Gathered from the only three places that can actually answer: the bridge,
          Ollama, and OpenHands. A source we cannot reach is named as unreachable rather than
          shown as empty — "nothing running" and "cannot see" are different facts.

        

        

      

    


    

      

        
⌨️ Terminal

        
Run Prime Agent, Kimi, Hermes, Oh My Pi, Grok, Goose, Claude Code or Codex
          right here, next to the reasoning that produced the prompt. These same CLIs stay available
          in every model picker — this is an addition, not a replacement. Requires the bridge (v3+),
          because a browser cannot spawn a process.

        

        

          
          
          
        

        

          

          
          
        

        

        

        
      

    




    

      

        
🏢 Virtual Office

        
The swarm, as a room. Nothing here is simulated: a character typing at a
          desk means that bot really holds that task, two characters talking means that message
          really was sent, and a red mark over someone's head means something destructive really
          is waiting on your approval. When the swarm is idle, the room is idle — that is the
          feature, not a bug.

        

          
          
          
          
          
          
          
        

        

          
        

        

      

      

        
🎯 Steer the team

        
One standing direction that governs everything the office does, and a
          mode that decides how literally to take it. The mode changes the prompt every worker
          receives — it is not a filter applied afterwards.

        

        

        
        

          
          
          
        

      

      

        
🧑‍💼 Manager

        
A reasoning model that plans and delegates but never builds. It is the
          only role allowed to create tasks — if every agent could invent work the board would
          fill with overlapping duplicates, and the artifact locks would spend their time
          refusing them. It is told that two tasks must never touch the same file, because that
          is exactly what stalls a swarm.

        

          
          
          
        

        

        

      

      

        
🗂 Outputs

        
Everything the team actually produced. These are the same artifacts the
          lock system governs, so this is a view of real work rather than a second copy that
          drifts out of date. Click the Outputs shelf in the office to open it too.

        

          
          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🏗 Office design

        
The room is data, so a theme changes the layout, the palette and which
          fixtures exist — not just the colours. Everything below persists.

        

          
          
        

        

          
          
        

        

        
Fixtures

        

      

      

        
👤 Who is doing what

        

      

    


    

      

        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
      


      

        

          
🤖 Bots

          
A standing team rather than one assistant. Each bot has a name, a role
            and its own model, and they can hand work to each other — every handoff is recorded
            as a message so the collaboration is readable after the fact instead of being an
            opaque multi-agent blob.

          

            
            
            
            
            
          

          
          

        

        

          
▶ Run a collaboration

          
Give the team a goal. Bots take turns, and a bot may address another by
            name to hand over — that handoff appears in Messages as
            Susan → Randy. Rounds are capped, because a team that can
            talk forever will.

          

            
            
            
            
          

          

        

      


      

        

          
🕸 Bot Network — the board

          
A swarm's failures are coordination failures, not reasoning ones, so
            these are enforced in code rather than asked for in a prompt. A bot cannot write to
            an artifact it has not claimed, cannot claim one another bot holds, and cannot commit
            a write built from a version that has since moved. Refusals are logged with the
            reason, because a bot told "no" without a reason simply retries.

          

          

            
            
            
            
          

          

        

        

          
🔒 Held for approval

          
Anything a bot proposes that deletes, overwrites, ships, contacts real
            people, moves money or changes access is stopped here first. The classifier is
            deliberately over-eager: a false positive costs one click, a false negative costs
            data.

          

        

        

          
📄 Artifacts

          

        

        

          
📜 Network log

          

        

      

      

        

          
💬 Message feed

          
Every message between bots, in order. This is the collaboration record —
            who asked whom for what, and what came back.

          

            
            
          

          

        

      


      

        

          
📞 Call

          
A standing meeting with the bots you invite. You speak by typing; they
            answer in turn and, with speech on, read their replies aloud through the browser's own
            voice engine — no audio model and no audio ever leaves this machine.

          

            

          

          

            
            
            
            
            
          

          

          

            
            
          

        

      


      

        

          
👁 Monitors

          
Watch a page and get told what actually changed — not that a byte moved.
            Each check fetches the page, reduces it to visible text, diffs it against the last
            snapshot, and (optionally) has a model summarise the change in a sentence. Fetching
            needs the bridge for anything that does not send CORS headers.

          

            
            
            
            
          

          
          

        

      


      

        

          
📰 News

          
Latest items on a topic, pulled through whichever web access is
            configured. Sources are shown per item — an item with no link is a model's
            recollection, not news, and is labelled as such.

          

            
            
            
          

          

        

      


      

        

          
🤖 OpenBot

          
CopilotKit's OpenBot (MIT) gives each AI coworker a real computer — a browser with
            real logins, a filesystem, tools — and governs it: every action is decided before it
            happens and recorded after. That is the same model as this app's Bot Network, so the two
            compose: OpenBot owns the machines and the audit trail, Glassbox Jet owns the room, the
            steering and the task board.

          
This needs the bridge, and that is not a workaround. OpenBot ships
            no CORS headers anywhere — a deliberate choice stated in its own server source, because
            it expects the app to reach /api on its own origin. A browser
            on this origin therefore cannot call it directly. Start the bridge from the Handoff tab
            first.

          

            
            
            
          

          

            
            Running locally with
              OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true? Leave this blank.
          

          

        

        

          
🖥 Coworker computers

          
What each coworker's machine is actually doing. Read-only here on
            purpose — navigating and clicking are actions, and actions belong behind the
            approval gate rather than one click away in a status panel.

          

        

        

          
📜 Audit trail

          
OpenBot's trail is append-only and nothing can delete a row, which makes
            it a better record than anything this app keeps in browser storage — so it is read,
            never copied.

          

            
            
          

          

        

      

      

        

          
🔗 Hermes Agent

          
Nous Research's open-source agent exposes an OpenAI-compatible
            /v1/chat/completions and a /api/jobs
            REST surface, so a self-hosted instance can be driven directly from here. Point this at
            your instance and it probes both before claiming anything works.

          

            
            
            
            
          

          

        

        

          
✉️ AgentMail

          
Real inboxes for agents — api.agentmail.to/v0.
            Bots can be given an address, read their threads and reply. The key is stored in this
            browser only.

          

            
            
            
          

          

        

        

          
🤖 Hermes Bot Mode

          

        

      

    


    

      

        
🎓 Study

        
Everything the harness did — reasoning traces, builder actions, tool calls
          and what came out — read back by a model and turned into an assessment you can act on.
          Three questions: is this combination actually working, what would work better, and does
          the better answer fit the budget you set.

        

          
          
          
        

        

          
          
          
          
        

        
The ceiling is what a recommendation may
          assume you would spend. If the genuinely better setup costs more than that, the
          assessment says so explicitly rather than quietly proposing something you cannot afford
          — or quietly withholding it.

📦 Asset library

          
Free, genuinely reusable 3D asset sources — every entry here is CC0 or
            an explicitly permissive licence, with the licence named. Pick the packs you want and
            the game builder is told to use those specifically rather than inventing geometry.

🖼 Image → three.js

          
Describe or upload a reference, and get procedural three.js that
            reconstructs it in code — a mesh you can read, diff and edit, rather than an opaque
            binary. Generation needs an image-capable model; the reconstruction step works from
            any image you can show it.

          

            
            
            
          

          

            
            
          

          

        

      

      

        

          
🌍 Open-source world systems

          
Procedural systems you can drop into a scene — oceans, grass, trees,
            fluids, whole planets. These are real repositories with real licences, not a curated
            list of screenshots. Each entry says what it needs to run, because several are
            WebGPU-only and will render nothing at all on a browser without it.

          

        

        

          
🧪 Recipes — combining them

          
Order matters more than choice. An ocean that does not know the terrain
            height cannot mask its own foam line; grass instanced before chunking re-uploads its
            buffers on every LOD change. These are the sequences that work.

          

        

        

          
♻️ Source loop — feed a repo to the agents

          
Pulls the real files out of a repository through your GitHub
            connector and hands them to a model with a concrete job. A model's recollection of a
            library is exactly the confident, stale answer this app exists to avoid — Poseidon is
            WebGPU/TSL, and a model working from memory will write you WebGL that cannot run
            against it. Bounded: 14 files, 120k characters.

          

            
            
            
            
          

          

          

        

        

          
📚 Free asset & texture sources

          

            
          

          

        

        

          
🛠 AAA tooling & methods

          
What actually makes a detailed map run: instancing, LOD, culling,
            streaming, compression, baking, profiling.

          

        

      


      

        

          
⚛ React Three Fiber

          
R3F is not a stronger engine — it uses three.js. It is an
            orchestration layer, and what it buys you is architecture: an agent can change the
            inventory system without mangling the renderer. What it costs you is the single file
            you can AirDrop and open, because it needs npm and a build step. This tells you which
            of three paths actually fits your scene rather than converting blindly.

          

        

        

          
📦 Generate a project

          

            
            
            
            
            
          

          

            
            
            
          

          
The current editor scene is embedded, so what you
            built here survives the conversion rather than starting from an empty canvas.

          

        

        

          
🧱 Vanilla architecture

          
You can take the good parts without React. Rapier and Zustand both work
            in vanilla, and reorganising a monolith into real systems often helps more than
            converting its rendering syntax to JSX.

          

        

      


      

        

          
🎮 Build a game with these assets

          
The builder is told which asset packs to use, with their real CDN or
            download URLs and their licences, and is instructed to load them rather than
            substitute primitives. Anything it cannot source, it must say so about rather than
            silently swapping in a cube.

          
          

            
            
            
          

          

        

      

    


    

      

        
🗂 Projects

        
Separate desktops. Switching swaps the whole working context — workspace
          files, Brain, chats, traces, long-horizon manifest, goldens and tasks — and switching
          back restores it exactly. Your API keys, providers, theme, skills and prompts are
          shared across every project, because those are about you rather than about a project.

        

          
          
        

        

      

      

        
OpenRouter connection

        
        

          
          
          
        

        

        

          
          
        

        
Provider-agnostic — point Base URL at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint to add more providers later.

      

      

        
Defaults

        

          
          
        

        

          
          
        

        

      

      

        
🖥 Ollama — local models, free to run

        
Every pulled model joins the pickers as ollama/<name>. Use one as your Builder and Relay costs drop to zero — the frontier model still does all the thinking.

        

          
          
        

        
not scanned yet

        
Advanced — address & how detection works

          
          
Connect probes 127.0.0.1, localhost and [::1] together and keeps whichever one actually answers, because macOS often runs two Ollama servers at once — the desktop app on IPv6 and a terminal ollama serve on IPv4. localhost resolves to IPv6 first, so a terminal-set OLLAMA_ORIGINS is frequently never reached.

        

      

      

        
🔑 Providers 

        
Bring your own keys — a Z.ai GLM coding plan, Moonshot/Kimi, xAI, DeepSeek direct, or any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Most of these servers don't send CORS headers, so a browser page can't call them directly; leave route via local bridge on and the bridge forwards the request for you.

        

      

      

        
🔗 Claude Code / Codex — use your subscription instead of API credits

        
A web page cannot read your Claude or ChatGPT subscription credentials, and relaying a subscription through a third-party app isn't something the providers allow. What is fine: driving the CLIs you already installed and signed in to, on your own machine. glassbox-bridge.mjs does exactly that — it shells out to claude and codex and speaks the same streaming format as everything else here, so those models behave identically to API ones.

        

          
          
        

        
not scanned yet

        
How to start it

          
In Terminal, from the folder holding these files:

          
node glassbox-bridge.mjs
            

          
It needs whichever CLIs you want to use already on your PATH and logged in (claude for Claude Code, codex for Codex). The bridge never sees or stores your credentials — the CLIs handle their own auth.

          
          
Connect scans ports 8791, 8792, 8890, 9137 and 8787 and keeps whichever one answers. Your AI Harness already holds 8787, which is why the bridge defaults off it.

        

      

      

        
Output completeness

        
        
When a model stops because it hit the token ceiling (finish_reason: length), Glassbox Jet automatically asks it to resume from the exact cut-off point and stitches the pieces together — up to 5 times. This is what stops long games and long reasoning from arriving half-written. Leave this on.

      

      

        
Install on iPhone / Mac

        
This is a single file with zero dependencies. On iPhone: open it in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen for a full-screen app. On Mac: open the file directly, or Chrome → Install. To use it on your phone from anywhere, drop GlassBox.html in iCloud Drive or any static host — no server needed.

      

      

        
Data

        
Reasoning traces can contain sensitive content — everything stays on your device. Use scrub-on-export before sharing.
